posts.title: The Library of Babel: Jorge Luis Borges and the Search for Meaning
posts.description: In his 1941 fable The Library of Babel, Borges imagines a library containing every possible book: from random strings of nonsense to the genuine explanation for existence. The problem is, in this world of pure information, humanity can’t identify meaning amid the junk.

posts.title: 2 Ideas that Changed My World: Jack Maden Interview, The Philosophy Prescription
posts.description: My interview with Ten Have on how our deepest personal concerns can find expression and consolation in philosophy, as well as two philosophical ideas that changed my world.

posts.title: Manufacturing Nostalgia: Paula Sweeney on Longing for How Life Once Felt
posts.description: Rather than a desire to recover the actual events of the past, philosopher Paula Sweeney argues nostalgia is primarily about seeking refuge in previously felt emotions. Politicians and marketers routinely invoke feelings from a fabled past to drive action in the present.
